artifacts.summary: Measured current SKILL.md/orchestrate.md/eager-load byte counts against Stage A targets, found a reusable ceiling-config+severity-gate precedent (claudemd-size-budget.json), identified a load-bearing hazard where warn-tier findings would spuriously trip the inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint's new-findings diff, derived a schema-accurate per-cycle growth estimate (~850-1010 B/task), and located the stale Context Flatness prose to correct.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's inter-cycle redeploy checkpoint (orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh) diffs the SET of `^FINDING ` lines from `verify-deploy.sh --findings` before/after a redeploy (deploy-baseline-lib.sh), not the exit code. warn() and fail() both emit indistinguishable FINDING lines, so any warn-tier gate whose default finding text embeds a value that changes run-to-run (a byte count, a timestamp) will register as a spurious 'new finding' on nearly every redeploy and wrongly trip defer_reason:deploy_checkpoint. Any new gate must pass a normalized, value-free 3rd argument to warn()/fail() (the pattern fail()'s own header comment already documents) and print the live number only to stderr outside the finding text.

context/config/claudemd-size-budget.json + check_claudemd_size_budget() in check-extension-docs.sh + SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE env-var default is this repo's reusable pattern for 'small ceiling config in source store, severity toggled by an env-var default a human flips (not auto-promoted by a persisted counter)'. Reuse this shape directly for any new byte-ceiling gate rather than inventing a new config format or building N-consecutive-deploys auto-promotion machinery.
